comparator.name: International Sociology
comparator.sourceNotes: The English International Sociology track comprises sixty credits per year. The retained Culture in Comparative Perspective major is first-listed and continues the programme’s comparative cultural identity independently of UCR fit. Its twelve-credit second-year Culture research project and twelve-credit Culture thesis use the appropriate variants. The non-exchange final year combines a twelve-credit placement, eighteen genuinely open credits, twelve restricted credits selected as Globalization and Social Risks plus Global Migration, and six-credit Social Philosophy. The two electives are the first two subjects in the public Social Risks list and belong to the non-selected major. Thesis entry requires all propaedeutic subjects and sixty postpropaedeutic credits. The placement needs an approved plan and contract before starting and at least 336 hours. Zero-credit GROW is not added to the total.
components: Academic Skills 2 follows Skills 1. Skills 3 builds on earlier skills and research methods, with introductory statistics alongside. The first-year project applies these foundations.
The twelve-credit Culture research project applies earlier quantitative and qualitative methods to a complete sociological group investigation, report and presentation.
Sociological and Historical Perspectives on Identities
A Cultural Sociological Approach to Climate Change
Families in Context: How families define us

This non-exchange pathway requires at least 336 hours in a relevant organisation. An approved learning plan and signed contract are required before starting. Supervision and a reflective report complete the assessment; no particular host is assumed.
Eighteen credits remain open for a minor, free electives or a permitted combination. No particular package is imposed.
Selected as a six-credit restricted choice from the other major. It examines globalisation, poverty, social protection and changing social risks.
Selected as the second six-credit restricted choice from the other major. It examines migration theories, labour and refugee flows, and connections with sending and receiving societies.
Bachelor's Thesis Sociology Culture in Comparative Perspective

The twelve-credit Culture thesis is an individual empirical sociological study with a proposal, article-style paper, peer feedback and symposium presentation. Entry requires all first-year courses and at least 60 postpropaedeutic EC. Both earlier years are completed before the normal Spring thesis; Autumn entry is exceptional.

routeSelection.basis: International Sociology explicitly uses an international and comparative perspective and offers two majors. Culture in Comparative Perspective directly continues that defining comparative identity and is listed first in the official curriculum. It is selected independently of UCR fit.

core: Sociological theories of social interaction, institutions, cohesion and social change
Social inequality, poverty, exclusion, welfare and urban life
Qualitative, quantitative and mixed sociological research using surveys, statistics and projects
Relationships among individuals, groups, institutions, society and public policy
Academic sociological craft and independent research culminating in a thesis
adjacent: Public policy, institutions and collective responses to social problems
Migration, culture, family and identities in comparative perspective
Climate, health, work and sustainability as social risks in changing societies
questions: What structures and mechanisms produce inequality and changing social problems?
How do institutions, culture and collective action reproduce or change social relations?
How can qualitative and quantitative evidence explain social patterns and change?

blocks: Sociology, cultural inquiry and complementary methods

Both develop literature evaluation, academic argument, research questions and scholarly writing. UCR combines these with personal development and civic collaboration; Tilburg specifically develops sections of sociological research articles.
Both develop empirical design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling and introductory analysis. UCR additionally includes a substantial team data-collection project.

Both address questionnaire construction and quantitative analysis. UCR designs and pilots a psychological survey and analyses reliability and relationships; Tilburg additionally teaches scale validity, PCA, factor analysis and psychometric evaluation in a dedicated methods course.

Both develop data retrieval, preparation, recoding, analysis, visual/tabular presentation and interpretation. UCR has broader tabular, spatial and text-data workflows; Tilburg explicitly connects these skills to sociological questions.

Both analyse socially and historically constructed identities in relation to power. UCR focuses on Indigenous history and cultural resurgence; Tilburg compares class, gender, ethnicity and national identities.

Both develop normative reflection on responsibility and justice. UCR supplies ethical theories and practical moral argument; Tilburg specifically examines power, group agency, social responsibility and epistemic injustice.
Both examine political institutions, actors and behaviour through political-science concepts and comparative analysis.
Both introduce sociological questions, concepts, classical theories and relations among individuals, institutions and societies.
Both develop qualitative design, interviewing, coding, thematic interpretation, ethics and research reporting.
Both develop contemporary sociological theory and use it to interpret society; UCR also emphasises colonial and postcolonial criticism.

Both analyse how public spheres and institutions define, contest and respond to social problems. UCR focuses on civil society, trust, solidarity and social repair; Tilburg explicitly studies competing problem owners, historical framing, media and the distinction between social, sociological and policy problems.
Both examine social cognition, attitudes, influence, groups and interpersonal behaviour using empirical psychological evidence.

Both develop ANOVA, correlation, multivariable regression and logistic analysis with software, model choice and interpretation. UCR applies these to behavioural/health evidence; Tilburg integrates them into the sociological methods sequence.

Both examine how climate narratives, values, power and social positions shape public meaning and responses. UCR centres communication and intervention; Tilburg compares denial, action and adaptation through cultural sociology.

Both study culture, reproduction and unequal power through theory and empirical materials. UCR focuses on racial representation and American media histories; Tilburg surveys modern cultural-sociological classics, individualisation, secularisation and cultural reproduction.
Other disciplinary requirements and open choice
Literature searching and critical reading support several courses, whose strongest placements are with research writing and empirical methods; none is counted again as this introductory skills unit.
Statistical inference is taught within the selected methods and advanced analysis courses, whose strongest placements are elsewhere. No course is counted twice.
Related theory and methods appear elsewhere; no additional selected course is counted as this separate disciplinary requirement.
Several selected courses conduct empirical research, but none is counted a second time as the separate first-year Sociology project.
Methodological and ethical reflection is present, but no selected course supplies a dedicated social-science philosophy-of-science unit.
The twelve-credit Culture group investigation is a separate required research experience, beyond the methods already aligned.

Social psychology and gendered and Indigenous histories offer family-related insights, but no selected course centres the full European family-sociology programme of intergenerational inequality, family change and macro-context.
A required 336-hour sociological placement is not a scheduled UCR course; no host or substitute internship is assumed.
Eighteen open credits remain unspecified, with no named minor or course package invented.
Transnational institutions and social-risk courses contribute related perspectives, but no additional course is counted as this dedicated globalisation/social-protection unit.
International institutions, histories and rights illuminate migration, but no additional selected course centres migration flows and sending/receiving societies.
The individual empirical Culture thesis remains compulsory. Optional UCR independent research is separately shown outside the scheduled 180 EC.

selection.assessment: The closest programme uses the complete available UCR sociology sequence and implements the selected international-comparative culture route. The global-social-risks and international-inequality/policy directions are independently supported by generator-eligible programme interests and the official curriculum, produce substantively different course choices, and pass feasibility and pairwise distinctness. Production therefore stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: UCR combines sociological theory and research with cultural, political, health and environmental perspectives. Tilburg provides a prescribed methods sequence, a twenty-four-credit major, a required placement and an individual sociology thesis. The relationships shown are partial.

audience.programmeDescription: International Sociology at Tilburg studies social relations, cultural differences, inequality and change through a comparative perspective. This example follows Culture in Comparative Perspective, selects Globalization and Social Risks and Global Migration as restricted electives, and retains open study, a placement and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR can develop a cultural and identity focus, a global social-risk focus or an international inequality and policy focus. Its courses offer substantial theory, empirical research and interdisciplinary study. Tilburg has a more prescribed sociology sequence and major, with a compulsory placement and thesis. Relationships shown are partial.
